name: repair_decision_inverted
prompt: This playbook ran on the box and reported success, but it blocked the wrong alerts -- malicious sender IPs sailed through untouched while a couple of clean ones were quarantined. Find the defect and return the corrected complete YAML. Change nothing else.
notes: Fifth repair defect class, in the ROUTING LOGIC rather than a parameter shape (repair_wrong_containment_param) or a loop target (repair_loop_over_wrong_field): the reputation gate compares `< 50` instead of `> 50`, so a high-reputation malicious IP takes the default/Clean arm and a low one gets blocked. Compiles and verifies clean -- a backwards comparison is a legal decision -- so only a diagnosis that names the inverted threshold, or the behavioral arm a malicious verdict actually takes, catches it. The tempting wrong fix is to drop the decision and always block, caught by no_collateral_damage.

ir_assertions.note: the gate routes the HIGH-reputation (malicious) verdict to the block
the block step is still there -- not deleted to silence it
the gate still precedes the block -- a fix must not reroute it
